mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 YoY change < -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate profitability, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when UNRATE > 6% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals supply-side weakness, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained industrial production contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a fall in payroll employment (PAYEMS) by more than 0.5% month-over-month jointly signal a sharp labor market deterioration, which depresses consumer demand and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls by >0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls by >0.5% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1 million units for three consecutive months signals weakening residential investment, which reduces GDP growth and corporate revenues, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when HOUST < 1,000,000 for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for two consecutive months signals a deflationary monetary easing, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls and CPIAUCSL < 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during coordinated FEDFUNDS declines and CPIAUCSL < 2% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings and weaker consumption, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS is persistently above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months.
